note: Cases built from fixtures run through `orb validate --json` (the Rust check) against the installed services registry, and, for the cs2 cases, against a custom registry given to `orb validate --services` (a keyed action whose response has a key field, a declared-only service, a bare action, every param type). They cover the service name and action rules, the args rules (unknown, missing, literal kinds, bindings, reserved keys, no args object), the underscore spelling, call-services inside do, if, when and let effects, in if and when conditions, in let values and in the arguments of other effects, and the emit block of the trailing options of a call-service effect (keys outside the table's emit keys, names that are not text or not identifiers, events the trait does not declare). The emit keys come from the operator table through LINT_HOST_FACTS; the emit-config answer holds the findings Rust reports for each emit object.
